transformations.description: Compared acid and alkaline-treated corn stalks for biogas production, revealing that the acid pretreatment inhibited the co-digestion process, possibly because the lignin content presented a sharper reduction with the hydrogen peroxide treatment than with sulfuric acid.

references.title: Sustainable valorization of corn biomass: a circular approach to bioenergy and bioproducts | Systems Microbiology and Biomanufacturing | Springer Nature Link
references.snippet: The work developed by Liu and collaborators (Liu et al. 2018) also focused on biogas production. The authors used four anaerobic digesters fed with corn husks under different temperature conditions (35 °C, 38 °C, 41 °C, and 44 ºC), achieving 810 mL·L−1·d−1 in the reactor operated at 44 °C. Additionally, Venturin and co-workers (2018), compared acid and alkaline-treated corn stalks for biogas production, revealing that the acid pretreatment inhibited the co-digestion process, possibly because the lignin content presented a sharper reduction with the hydrogen peroxide treatment than with sulfuric acid. The authors recommended a hydrogen peroxide treatment, as this strategy increased the biogas final volume by 22% and reduced the digestion time by one third. Biohydrogen can also be obtained [...] manipulated corn stalks with biocompatible ionic liquids and achieved a bioethanol yield of 84%. [...] Other than SAF, biogas can also be obtained from the corn processing chain. Sumardiono et al. (2022) used corn stalks with cattle manure for biogas production. In this study, the authors investigated the effect of pretreatment on raw biogas yield and concluded that 20-mesh stalks with the addition of Effective Microorganisms (EM-4) at 7% v/v yielded a maximum daily rate of 19.86 L/kg, reaching a total production of 215.77 L/kg/day of biogas.

references.snippet: and reduce the exploitation of natural resources. This review highlights the potential for juice waste valorization, providing insights into extraction methods, characterization of bioactives, and potential industrial applications. Future research should focus on optimizing extraction processes and expanding the application of bioactives to achieve sustainable waste management and economic growth. [...] AP also contains polyphenolic compounds that have antioxidant properties and function as antimicrobial, anticancer, and antidiabetic agents. Therefore, there is considerable potential for technological applications in the pharmaceutical, biomedical, cosmetic, and food industries . The polyphenolic compounds in AP are extracted using various organic solvents, such as methanol, ethanol, and acetone . Bai et al.  conducted a study on AP obtained from industrial sources. They observed a radical scavenging rate of 90.96±10.23%, ABTS radical scavenging of 89.78±6.54%, and a strong ferric reducing power of 8.30±0.71 µmol TE kg−1 equivalents dry AP. Furthermore, the AP extracts exhibited antibacterial activity against _Escherichia coli_, _Staphylococcus aureus_, and _Salmonella enterica_, with [...] Morphological and structural analyses highlighted the impact of the extraction process on the cashew apple bagasse and the resulting pectins. The application of pressure-enhanced porosity in the pectin structure improved thermal stability, significantly reducing the material's hemicellulose fraction. The Ecoscale Environmental Assessment scored 89.75 for pectin extraction and 93 for TPC recovery, surpassing other extraction methods reported in the literature. These findings contribute to the valorization of agro-industrial waste and the development of high-value products from cashew apple bagasse, offering significant potential for the processing industry.

references.title: Olive mill wastes: from wastes to resources - PMC
references.snippet:
OMSW spreading on agricultural surfaces has also been adopted as an operationally simple and economically feasible valorization method. The composition of pomace is relatively similar to that of organic amendments, and thus can be used for agronomic purposes (Toscano and Montemurro 2012). Other than being economical and easily practicable management method for olive mill operator, it has been reported conferring considerable benefits for soil characteristics and crops productivity. Kavdir and Killi (2007) demonstrated that soil amendment with pomace improves its water holding capacity, structure, and stability, making it less susceptible to erosion.
